title: refactor: declare community modality behavior
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds one shared modality specification for catalog category, inputs, outputs, routes, and pricing fields
- Uses the same specification in validation, dashboard controls, and model definitions
- Replaces five endpoint helpers and the nested community registry branch with one resolver
- Preserves transcription route restrictions and image-edit detection

Tests:
- `npm run typecheck` in Enter and Gen
- 6 community endpoint policy tests
- 9 focused community modality/catalog integration tests

gist.headline: One map for the meadow
gist.blurb: Community models now grow from one shared little field guide instead of several nearly-identical ones. Polli put the routes, controls, pricing, and validation on the same page; remarkably, they now agree.
gist.summary: Community endpoint behavior is now declared in one shared modality specification used for catalog categories, inputs, outputs, routes, pricing fields, validation, dashboard controls, and model definitions, while retaining transcription-route restrictions and image-edit detection.
gist.impact: Community model listings and endpoints now draw their rules from the same resolver, making route access, dashboard controls, pricing metadata, transcription handling, and image-edit recognition more consistent.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy garden field guide that unifies several labeled paths—catalog, routes, inputs, outputs, pricing, and validation—into one map. Polli, wearing a tiny cartographer hat, points at the shared map while the eager CRT Monitor Robot happily connects glowing code-vines from the map to a community-model garden; include a small transcription microphone path and an image-edit paintbrush path to represent the preserved special handling.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings, wearing a tiny cartographer hat and studying one shared garden map labeled in simple pixel text “MODALITIES”; a cute chunky CRT monitor robot connects code-vines from the map to flower beds for catalog, routes, pricing, a microphone, and a paintbrush. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, with blooming code-plants and subtle CRT glow; nostalgic but beautiful, emotionally warm.
